subject: lulcw:Piezometer
definition_comparison: GW_Well: a shaft or hole sunk, dug or drilled into the Earth to observe, extract or inject water (SAWGraph's rendering of GWML2, imports/gwml2_hyfo_terms.ttl); a lulcw:Piezometer is a BSS monitoring point of the network
counterexample_considered: Some monitoring points are springs (Fontestramar 10795X0001/S, Source de la Tirounère, Source Sainte-Cécile, Source Clots de Rhodes): not drilled wells, so no subclass

subject: lulcw:Piezometer
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: Withdrawn 2026-11-06: the springs of the network are lulcw:Piezometer instances

subject: lulcw:Piezometer
definition_comparison: hyfo:WaterWell: a water well, with focus on the hole/shaft itself; a lulcw:Piezometer is a BSS monitoring point
counterexample_considered: The springs of the network are not wells

subject: lulcw:MonitoringStation
definition_comparison: GW_MonitoringSite: site of observation related to groundwater; a lulcw:MonitoringStation is a station of the ADES groundwater-level network
counterexample_considered: A station hosted by a spring is still a monitoring site: none found
reviewer: Claude (2026-10-24, rechecked 2026-11-06), to review by Assil

subject: lulcw:hostedBy
definition_comparison: gwMonitoringHost: identifies the feature hosting the site, e.g. a well, spring, lake or stream; lulcw:hostedBy links a station to its piezometer
counterexample_considered: A spring host is explicitly allowed by GWML2: none

subject: lulcw:HydrogeologicalUnit
definition_comparison: GW_HydrogeoUnit: any soil or rock unit or zone that by virtue of its hydraulic properties has a distinct influence on the storage or movement of groundwater; a BD LISA entity is one
counterexample_considered: An impermeable BD LISA entity still influences the movement of groundwater (GW_AquiferUnit includes confining beds): none found

subject: lulcw:ConfiningUnit
definition_comparison: Entailed through lulcw:HydrogeologicalUnit
counterexample_considered: None

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: GW_Aquifer: a body of earth material that contains (or potentially contains) sufficient saturated permeable material to yield significant quantities of water to wells and springs; the written mapping rule types the alluvium units as alluvial aquifers
counterexample_considered: A locally confined alluvial unit (CQ14) is still an aquifer: none found

subject: lulcw:KarstAquifer
definition_comparison: As above; the written rule types the karst units as karst aquifers
counterexample_considered: None found

subject: lulcw:MultilayerAquiferSystem
definition_comparison: GW_AquiferSystem: a body of permeable and poorly permeable material that functions regionally as a water-yielding unit (two or more permeable beds separated by confining beds); the Pliocene multilayer (671AA00) by the written rule
counterexample_considered: None found

subject: lulcw:ConfiningUnit
definition_comparison: An impermeable mapped unit is not an aquifer
counterexample_considered: Its confining role is local; neither GW_Aquifer nor GW_ConfiningBed is asserted

subject: lulcw:monitors
definition_comparison: tapsAquifer: identifies the aquifer a well taps (no domain or range declared); lulcw:monitors links a piezometer to the unit it monitors
counterexample_considered: A spring monitors the unit it drains: consistent

subject: lulcw:pumpsFrom
definition_comparison: As above; lulcw:pumpsFrom links an abstraction facility to the unit it pumps from
counterexample_considered: None found

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: SWEET's Aquifer is broader and differently axiomatised
counterexample_considered: No subclass or equivalence asserted

subject: lulcw:KarstAquifer
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: As above

subject: lulcw:MultilayerAquiferSystem
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: As above

subject: lulcw:ConfiningUnit
definition_comparison: SWEET's Aquitard: a confining bed; a mapped impermeable unit is a candidate
counterexample_considered: As above

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: Confinement is a local assessment (CQ14)
counterexample_considered: Parts of an alluvial unit can be confined under a clay cover

subject: lulcw:Watercourse
definition_comparison: HY_River: a body of surface water, participating in a hydrographic network, that permanently or temporarily flows; a lulcw:Watercourse is a river identified by its BD Carthage code
counterexample_considered: A canal coded as a watercourse would not qualify: the graph's watercourses are the gauged and documented rivers, and canal reaches carry no watercourse

subject: lulcw:RiverReach
definition_comparison: HY_FlowPath realizes a catchment as a path connecting its inflow and outflow; a river reach is a mapped segment of the network between two nodes
counterexample_considered: The graph holds no catchment that a reach would realise: a close match, not a subclass

subject: lulcw:HydrographicReach
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: Withdrawn 2026-11-06 (Codex review, R3): a canal reach conveys diverted water across catchments and realises none

subject: lulcw:CanalReach
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: A canal reach realises no catchment

subject: lulcw:SurfaceWaterBody
definition_comparison: HY_WaterBody: water standing in a depression or flowing in a channel; a WFD river water body is a management delimitation of stretches
counterexample_considered: None needed: the meanings differ

subject: hyf:HY_River
definition_comparison: Stated by the OGC definitions server (SKOS); kept as skos:broader
counterexample_considered: Rendered as rdfs:subClassOf until 2026-11-06, a local commitment withdrawn (Codex review, R3)

subject: hyf:HY_FlowPath
definition_comparison: Stated by the OGC definitions server (OWL)
counterexample_considered: None

subject: lulcw:HydrogeologicalUnit
definition_comparison: INSPIRE: a part of the lithosphere with distinctive parameters for water storage and conduction; lulcw: a hydrogeological entity of the BD LISA reference (level 3), aquifer or not
counterexample_considered: Every BD LISA entity is such a part of the lithosphere; the lulcw class is narrower (one national reference, one level), hence a close match and no equivalence

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: INSPIRE: a wet underground layer of water-bearing permeable rock or unconsolidated materials from which groundwater can be usefully extracted using a water well; lulcw: a BD LISA unit of recent or ancient alluvium
counterexample_considered: A mapped alluvial unit may be locally dry or unproductive; the INSPIRE concept requires usable extraction, so no subclass

subject: lulcw:KarstAquifer
definition_comparison: INSPIRE Aquifer as above; lulcw: a BD LISA unit whose medium is karstic
counterexample_considered: Karst is conduit-dominated rather than a 'layer of permeable rock'; close match only

subject: lulcw:MultilayerAquiferSystem
definition_comparison: INSPIRE: a collection of aquifers and aquitards which together constitute the environment of groundwater; lulcw: a unit of several permeable horizons separated, at least locally, by poorly permeable beds (the Pliocene 671AA00)
counterexample_considered: BD LISA maps the Pliocene as one entity, not as a collection of mapped aquifers and aquitards: the internal horizons are not individuated, so a close match

subject: lulcw:MultilayerAquiferSystem
definition_comparison: INSPIRE Aquifer: one water-bearing layer; the lulcw class is a system of several horizons
counterexample_considered: INSPIRE has the system concept (unlike SWEET, where the class is matched to Aquifer for want of a better target)

subject: lulcw:ConfiningUnit
definition_comparison: INSPIRE Aquiclude: an impermeable body of rock or stratum of sediment that acts as a barrier to the flow of groundwater; lulcw: a unit mapped as impermeable in BD LISA (nature 7)
counterexample_considered: 'Mapped as impermeable' is a cartographic statement; a mapped unit may leak locally, so a close match

subject: lulcw:ConfiningUnit
definition_comparison: INSPIRE Aquitard: a saturated but poorly permeable bed that impedes groundwater movement, i.e. BD LISA's semi-permeable units (nature 6), which are not lulcw:ConfiningUnit
counterexample_considered: 671AA00 is labelled semi-permeable at level 3 and is typed MultilayerAquiferSystem by the written rule, not ConfiningUnit (the SWEET alignment matches ConfiningUnit to Aquitard because SWEET has no closer class)

subject: lulcw:GroundwaterBody
definition_comparison: INSPIRE: a distinct volume of groundwater within an aquifer or system of aquifers, which is hydraulically isolated from nearby groundwater bodies; lulcw: a groundwater body of the Water Framework Directive, a management unit
counterexample_considered: WFD bodies are delineated for management and are not all hydraulically isolated (the FRDG351 sheet describes exchanges with neighbouring formations); close match only

subject: lulcw:AbstractionFacility
definition_comparison: INSPIRE ActiveWell: a well influencing the groundwater resources of the aquifer; lulcw: a BNPE reporting facility (ouvrage), which may group several boreholes or be a surface-water intake
counterexample_considered: Surface-water and canal intakes are AbstractionFacility instances and are not wells; lulcw has no class restricted to groundwater boreholes

subject: lulcw:MonitoringStation
definition_comparison: MonitoringInfrastructure: an infrastructure to monitor water; a lulcw:MonitoringStation is a station of the ADES groundwater-level network, hosted by a piezometer, whose head observations form a series
counterexample_considered: A station hosted by a spring (Fontestramar) still monitors water: none found

subject: lulcw:RiverGauge
definition_comparison: GaugingStation: an infrastructure to monitor and test terrestrial bodies of water; a lulcw:RiverGauge is a Hub'Eau hydrometric station that measures discharge at its own site
counterexample_considered: A gauge that records only stage still monitors a terrestrial water body: none found

subject: lulcw:Watercourse
definition_comparison: River: a natural flowing watercourse, usually freshwater, flowing towards an ocean, sea, lake or another river; a lulcw:Watercourse is a river identified by its BD Carthage code
counterexample_considered: The 22 watercourses of the v5 graph (release 2026-11-26) are natural rivers and streams (the Têt, Agly, Tech, Réart and their tributaries, the Aude); canal reaches carry no watercourse: none found

subject: lulcw:SurfaceWaterIntake
definition_comparison: Intake: an installation for obtaining water from a source of supply (river, lake, reservoir, and so on); a lulcw:SurfaceWaterIntake is a BNPE ouvrage withdrawing surface water, identified by its BNPE code
counterexample_considered: A BNPE ouvrage is a declaration record: one intake can be declared under several codes (the four replacement records named 'PRISE DANS LA BASSE PALAIS DE CONGRES', docs/canal_basins.md) and its coordinates can be coarse: a close match, not a subclass

subject: lulcw:Intake
definition_comparison: As above; a lulcw:Intake is an individual withdrawal point (borehole, well, spring or surface intake) of an abstraction facility
counterexample_considered: A spring withdrawal point is a natural outlet, not necessarily an installation: no subclass

subject: lulcw:CanalReach
definition_comparison: Channel: a passage of water flowing in an open conduit (subject to atmospheric pressure); a lulcw:CanalReach is a BD TOPO reach of nature canal, a mapped line between two network nodes
counterexample_considered: 50 of the 2,589 canal reaches of the dept-66 BD TOPO snapshot (2026-11-06) are mapped underground (position -1: siphons or piped sections, a closed conduit that SAREF4WATR calls a Pipe): no subclass

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: Aquifer: an underground layer of water-bearing permeable rock, rock fractures or unconsolidated materials, placed under StorageAsset (a water asset of a supply system); the written mapping rule types the alluvium units as alluvial aquifers
counterexample_considered: SAREF4WATR makes an aquifer a storage asset of a water system; a BD LISA unit is a mapped geological entity: close match only, as for SWEET

subject: lulcw:KarstAquifer
definition_comparison: As above; the karst units by the written rule
counterexample_considered: As above

subject: lulcw:MultilayerAquiferSystem
definition_comparison: As above; the Pliocene multilayer (671AA00) by the written rule
counterexample_considered: It holds several aquifers and confining beds: not one water-bearing layer

subject: lulcw:WaterUse
definition_comparison: WaterUse: the different uses of water; a lulcw:WaterUse is the declared BNPE use of an abstracted volume
counterexample_considered: SAREF4WATR's uses are those of supplied water (domestic, agriculture, recreation ...), the BNPE uses the purposes of abstraction (canal supply, energy): close only

subject: lulcw:DrinkingWaterUse
definition_comparison: Domestic: use of water for domestic purposes; lulcw:DrinkingWaterUse: abstraction for public drinking-water supply
counterexample_considered: Public supply also serves businesses and public buildings: close, not exact

subject: lulcw:IrrigationUse
definition_comparison: Agriculture: use of water for the farming of plants and livestock; lulcw:IrrigationUse: abstraction for agricultural irrigation
counterexample_considered: Livestock watering is agriculture but not irrigation: the SAREF4WATR concept is broader

subject: lulcw:IndustryUse
definition_comparison: Industry: use of water for industrial purposes; lulcw:IndustryUse: abstraction for industrial and economic uses
counterexample_considered: The BNPE category also holds non-industrial economic activities: close, not exact

subject: lulcw:RiverDischarge
definition_comparison: FlowRate: property indicating the rate of a water flow; lulcw:RiverDischarge: weekly mean discharge at a gauge (m3/s)
counterexample_considered: A discharge is a flow rate; close rather than exact because SAREF4WATR's flow properties serve supply networks and ours is a weekly mean at a river site

subject: lulcw:Piezometer
definition_comparison: Pit: a well or hole sunk in the ground to procure, store or drain water; a lulcw:Piezometer is a groundwater-level monitoring point
counterexample_considered: A piezometer observes water and procures, stores or drains none; some are springs

subject: lulcw:CropCode
definition_comparison: Crop: a collection of cultivated plants that is grown on a large scale commercially (with planting and harvest dates); lulcw:CropCode: a code of a parcel register's nomenclature
counterexample_considered: A code is a category of a nomenclature, a SAREF4AGRI crop the plants themselves: different kinds of things

subject: lulcw:WeatherCell
definition_comparison: WeatherStation: a sensor or system that measures weather conditions; lulcw:WeatherCell: a point of the SAFRAN 8 km reanalysis grid
counterexample_considered: A reanalysis grid cell is a spatial support for interpolated model outputs, not a measuring device

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: ENVO aquifer: an underground layer of water-bearing permeable rock or unconsolidated materials (gravel, sand, silt, or clay) from which groundwater can be usefully extracted using a water well; the written mapping rule types the alluvium units as alluvial aquifers (the reading of the gwml2:GW_Aquifer row)
counterexample_considered: A locally confined alluvial unit (CQ14) is still an aquifer: none found

subject: lulcw:KarstAquifer
definition_comparison: As above; the karst units by the written rule
counterexample_considered: None found

subject: lulcw:MultilayerAquiferSystem
definition_comparison: As above; ENVO has no aquifer system, and the Pliocene multilayer is typed as one by the written rule
counterexample_considered: It holds several aquifers and confining beds, not one layer: no subclass

subject: lulcw:Piezometer
definition_comparison: ENVO water well: a well which provides access to groundwater held in an aquifer (a well: a cylindrical hole, pit, or tunnel drilled or dug down to a depth from which water, oil, or gas can be pumped or brought to the surface); a lulcw:Piezometer is a BSS monitoring point
counterexample_considered: The springs of the network (Fontestramar 10795X0001/S and three others) are not wells, as for gwml2:GW_Well

subject: lulcw:Watercourse
definition_comparison: ENVO river: a stream which, through permanent or seasonal flow processes, moves from elevated land towards lower elevations through a definite channel and empties into a sea, lake or another river, or ends on land; a lulcw:Watercourse is a river identified by its BD Carthage code
counterexample_considered: The 22 watercourses of the v5 graph are natural rivers and streams, permanent or seasonal: none found

subject: lulcw:CanalReach
definition_comparison: ENVO canal: artificial watercourse with no flow or a controlled flow used for navigation, drainage or irrigation; a lulcw:CanalReach is one mapped reach of a canal
counterexample_considered: A reach is a segment of a canal, not the whole watercourse: close match only

subject: lulcw:LateralInflow
definition_comparison: ENVO groundwater flow: a water flow process during which water is transported through an aquifer; lulcw:LateralInflow: groundwater flowing into a unit from adjacent formations or from parts of the unit beyond a reference extent
counterexample_considered: Groundwater flow within a unit is not lateral inflow: the ENVO process is broader

subject: lulcw:GroundwaterBody
definition_comparison: ENVO groundwater: underground water located in pore spaces found in rock or unconsolidated deposits; a lulcw:GroundwaterBody is a Water Framework Directive management unit
counterexample_considered: A management delimitation is not the water itself, although the labels share a word (a trap for lexical matchers)

subject: lulcw:Watercourse
definition_comparison: SWEET River: a BodyOfWater (no textual definition); a lulcw:Watercourse is a river identified by its BD Carthage code
counterexample_considered: No definition to compare: close match only

subject: lulcw:CanalReach
definition_comparison: SWEET Canal: a BodyOfWater (no textual definition); a lulcw:CanalReach is one mapped reach of a canal
counterexample_considered: A reach is a segment of a canal: close match only

subject: lulcw:GroundwaterRecharge
definition_comparison: SWEET Recharge: a transport phenomenon whose realm is an aquifer (no textual definition); lulcw:GroundwaterRecharge: water reaching the saturated zone of a unit per unit of time, by any pathway
counterexample_considered: SWEET's is the phenomenon, ours the observable property (rate): close, not exact

subject: lulcw:DiffuseRecharge
definition_comparison: As above; lulcw:DiffuseRecharge: effective rainfall infiltrating where a unit is mapped at outcrop can raise its head
counterexample_considered: Recharge by rivers, canals or leakage is not diffuse: the SWEET phenomenon is broader

subject: lulcw:RiverDischarge
definition_comparison: SWEET StreamDischarge: a Discharge, a water flow (no textual definition); lulcw:RiverDischarge: weekly mean discharge at a gauge
counterexample_considered: Ours is a weekly mean at one site: close

subject: lulcw:SoilDrainage
definition_comparison: SWEET DeepPercolation: a Percolation (no textual definition); lulcw:SoilDrainage: SIM2 modelled water leaving the soil column (DRAINC), a recharge-related input
counterexample_considered: Ours is a model output, not the observed phenomenon: close

subject: lulcw:IrrigationUse
definition_comparison: SWEET Irrigation: a SoilCultivation with substance water (no textual definition); lulcw:IrrigationUse: abstraction for agricultural irrigation
counterexample_considered: SWEET's is the activity, ours the purpose of a declared volume: close
